title: Microburst kernel econ rundown
content:
Notes to self - microburst kernel econ rundown

Goal: sketch a compact, defensible subsidy and tiering heuristic for microbursts (short-lived high-concurrency spikes, often < 30s) that preserves latency SLOs and keeps unit economics sane.

Assumptions / environment
- Target SLO for interactive plans: 95th pct latency <= 300ms token gen on typical 8K-context conv.
- Typical model (open-llama variant) perf: ~120 tokens/sec per GPU core at 2K context; degraded with longer context.
- Dedicated reserved GPU cost (amortized): $1.60–$2.80 / GPU-hour depending on commitment. Spot/ephemeral ~50% lower but variable.
- Avg session: 18 turns, 1.6k tokens outgoing, 900 tokens incoming. Session median lifetime 6 minutes.

Quick back-of-envelope math (per-session amortization)
1) Token throughput -> GPU-time estimate
- Rough mapping: 1 GPU-hour ~= 432k generated tokens (120 tokens/sec * 3600).
- Cost per generated token (reserved): $2.00 / 432k ~= $0.00000463 (~0.000463 cents).
- For a session that generates 1.6k tokens: compute cost ~= $0.0074.

2) Microburst tail risk and concurrency overhead
- Microbursts require headroom: can pre-allocate warm slots or pay higher per-call queuing cost. If we reserve warm capacity equal to 10% of peak concurrent sessions, amortize warm-slot cost across all sessions.
- Example: 100k monthly sessions, average concurrency peak 600, reserve 60 GPUs warm. Monthly cost for 60 GPUs at $2/hr ~= 60 * 2 * 24 * 30 = $86400. Divide by 100k sessions => $0.864 per session if covered entirely by session count (too high). So must only credit a tiny fraction of sessions or cross-charge via higher-tier commit.

3) Micro-subsidy idea (cheap UX improvement)
- Offer small 'burst credits' on Starter/Explorer tiers: 20 bursts / month; define burst = 30s of prioritized processing capped at 1.2k generated tokens.
- Expected redemption: 3–8% of sessions for light users => amortized cost per user/month ~ $0.02–$0.08 (tolerable marketing subsidy).

4) Pricing levers and heuristics
- Burst credits vs committed warm slots: assign burst credits to lower tiers; require Dedicated/Committed customers to specify concurrency targets (we price warm slots as reserved GPUs * buffer factor).
- Tiering anchor: Explorer (payg-friendly): 2M tokens/month free-tier-ish cadence via credits; Builder: mid commit with cheaper per-token; Scale: enterprise commit with dedicated warm pool and SLA.

5) Cache-aware token accounting
- Distinguish regenerated tokens vs cached prefix hits. If >20% of tokens served from KV cache, bill at 25% of nominal token rate for those tokens (incentivizes caching-friendly UX). Track by route/model.

Open questions / TODOs
- How to measure flash redemption rate (need telemetry pipeline to record burst-credit use events with session ids).
- Sizing heuristics for warm pool: experiment with peak/90th-percentile concurrency smoothing and burst frequency.
- Impact of quantized variants: 4-bit -> ~1.6x throughput improvement, moves per-token cost down similarly. Add model-variant multipliers to unit-econ sim.

Experiment proposals
- Run a 6-week A/B: 10k new trial users, group A gets 10 burst credits, group B none. Track retention delta and burst redemption. Compute marginal RU (retention uplift) needed to justify $0.05 subsidy.
- Build quick sim: inputs = sessions/month, avg tokens/session, peak concurrency distribution, reserved-price, spot-mix, cache-hit-rate. Output = per-user subsidy budget for X% retention lift.

Rough heuristics summary (for product doc)
- Give tiny burst allowances to Starter to boost initial feel (cheap wins).
- For Builder, nudge toward predictable commit with cheaper per-token and explicit buffer-priced warm slots.
- For Scale, require concurrency SLAs and price dedicated warm pool explicitly; provide fallback model variants for graceful degradation.

Loose notes: record any PRs/CONFLUENCE pages created from this spade of experiments. Keep this as a working scratchpad; move final sim outputs to /shared_drives/product/optimize/pricing-sims when polished.

-- Maya
